findings.issue_text: app/views/embed/best.html.erb:6 — `<%- end if %>` is invalid Ruby syntax, causing template compilation to fail when rendering an existing embedded topic; replace it with `<%- end %>`.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:22 — Imported feed HTML is stored using `raw_html`, bypassing sanitization in `Post#cook` and allowing scripts and event handlers to survive as stored XSS on the forum’s origin; sanitize imported HTML before storing or rendering it.

app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35 — Unconditionally calling `i.content.scrub` aborts polling for valid RSS items that provide only `description`; use a description fallback and handle missing bodies.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:63–64 — Protocol-relative URLs such as `//cdn.example.com/image.jpg` are incorrectly treated as paths on the article host, breaking resources; resolve references against the article URL.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:63–64 — Path-relative URLs such as `images/photo.jpg` remain unresolved and load from the forum instead of the article’s location; resolve references against the article URL.

goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:22 — Imported feed HTML is stored using `raw_html`, bypassing sanitization in `Post#cook` and allowing scripts and event handlers to survive as stored XSS on the forum’s origin; sanitize imported HTML before storing or rendering it.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that in topic_embed.rb line 22, PostCreator is called with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. Looking at post.rb lines 131-133, when cook_method is raw_html, the cook method returns `raw` directly without any processing. The imported content from RSS feeds (poll_feed.rb) or remote URLs (import_remote via ruby-readability) is stored and rendered without sanitization. While ruby-readability limits tags to 'div p code pre h1 h2 h3 b em i strong a img', this still allows event handlers like onclick on those elements, and RSS content in poll_feed.rb uses CGI.unescapeHTML which doesn't sanitize. The content is then rendered with `raw post.cooked` in best.html.erb, creating a stored XSS vulnerability.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:63–64 — Protocol-relative URLs such as `//cdn.example.com/image.jpg` are incorrectly treated as paths on the article host, breaking resources; resolve references against the article URL.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at lines 63-64 in app/models/topic_embed.rb, the code checks `if src.present? && src.start_with?('/')` for img tags. Protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example.com/image.jpg` do start with '/' and would match this condition, causing them to be incorrectly prefixed with the article host (e.g., `http://eviltrout.com///cdn.example.com/image.jpg`). This is a real bug - the code should check for '//' to exclude protocol-relative URLs from the path-based URL rewriting.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:63–64 — Path-relative URLs such as `images/photo.jpg` remain unresolved and load from the forum instead of the article’s location; resolve references against the article URL.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the absolutize_urls method in app/models/topic_embed.rb lines 52-70, the code only handles URLs that start with '/' (checking `href.start_with?('/')` and `src.start_with?('/')`). Path-relative URLs like 'images/photo.jpg' (without a leading slash) would not match this condition and would remain unchanged. When rendered on the Discourse forum, these relative URLs would resolve against the forum's domain rather than the original article's domain, causing broken images/links. This is a real bug in the URL resolution logic.
